title: MRR GoldLabelSet
description: task-packets/N1-T02.yaml R1: a frozen gold standard for evidence-relation classification — the fixed set of correct answers against which a classifying system's VALIDITY is measured. WHY THIS LIVES HERE AND NOT UNDER schemas/ (corrected during the N1-T02 build, 2026-08-01): schemas/ is reserved for governed CONTRACT ENTITIES, and tests/contract/test_examples.py enforces that reservation — every file there must have a matching examples/*.example.json and a mrr.contracts Pydantic model, in lockstep. A gold label set is none of those things: it has no id/revision/status/signature lifecycle, it never enters the object store, and N1-T02 forbids packages/contracts/** on purpose. The packet originally placed it under schemas/; the repository's own test refused, and the repository was right. The precedent it now follows is CorpusEntry, whose module says the same thing of itself: 'validated only here (not schematized under schemas/)'. This document therefore describes an INPUT FILE, the way corpora/model-collapse/verification/agreement-crosswalk.v1.json is an input file — committed, hash-pinned, citable and contestable, but not a governed object. It is kept as JSON Schema rather than only as Python because another practice has to PRODUCE one of these: a machine-readable spec is what makes the commission checkable at its own end. Immutability is by VERSION, not by edit: mb-cls-v1 is never changed; a changed standard is mb-cls-v2, and scripts/check_gold_freeze.py fails when a registered version's bytes move. The order gate (labelled_at strictly after criteria_locked_at) is carried IN the data rather than asserted in prose, so a moved goal post is a refused run instead of a footnote — docs/design/2026-07-24-capability-roadmap-entwurf.md's N1 requirement 'Validierung erst nach Kriterien-Finalisierung (als Objekt-Zustand erzwingbar)'.

labelProvenance.description: WHO produced these labels, and under which act. Non-negotiable per the owner's decision of 2026-08-01: the criteria for 'better' are not set by the practice being measured, so a gold set that cannot say where its labels came from is not a standard. 'producing_practice' is the machine-checkable half; a set carrying the reserved value 'synthetic-fixture' is refused for real evaluation by the loader (N1-T02 R7) — quarantine by provenance, not by filename, because a filename can be copied.

producing_practice.description: Stable identifier of the practice or party that produced the labels — e.g. 'ulysses', 'ensemble', a urn:mrr:practice:... URN, or the reserved 'synthetic-fixture'.

account.description: Plain-language account of how the labels were made: blind or not, against which criteria, in which act or encounter.

encounter_id.description: The encounter register entry recording the act, when the labels came from a cross-practice exchange (e.g. 'enc-2026-006-...'). Null when they did not.

blind_to_measured_labels.description: Whether the labelling party was blind to the classifications being measured. False is permitted but must be stated: a non-blind rater is a confirmation, not an independent standard, and the report carries this through.

goldCase.description: One labelled case. The split between what a system may see and what only a scorer may see is enforced STRUCTURALLY at load time by benchmarks/meridianbench/harness.py's BenchmarkCase typing (E4-T07), not by this schema — this document is the on-disk form that the loader splits.

excerpt.description: The verbatim source text the classification is made against — never a third party's description of the source (corpora/README.md: 'Jeder claim_relevant_finding muss aus der Quelle selbst belegt sein').

excerpt_sha256.description: sha256 of the excerpt's UTF-8 bytes, so a drifted excerpt is detectable rather than silently re-read.

source_identifiers.description: How the source is found again. Shape mirrors CorpusEntry.identifiers.

claim_text.description: The claim the source is being related TO. Without it 'supports' has no object.

expected_relation.description: The correct answer. MUST be a member of the set's own declared 'categories'. Same vocabulary as CorpusEntry.evidence_relation, deliberately: the benchmark measures the decision the pipeline actually consumes.

expected_rationale.description: Why that relation is correct, in the labeller's own words. Scorer-visible only; it is the record that makes a disputed label arguable rather than merely asserted.

metadata.description: Free-text, human-readable reporting labels only (e.g. {'category': 'hedged finding'}). NEVER a side channel for anything a scorer needs — mirrors harness.BenchmarkCase.metadata's own restriction.

set_id.description: This frozen version's own name, e.g. 'mb-cls-v1'. Immutable: a changed standard gets a new set_id, never an edit.

categories.description: The declared label space, in an EXPLICIT order — the confusion matrix's axis order is taken from here, never from set/dict iteration (mrr.domain.agreement.confusion_matrix's own requirement).

criteria_version.description: Which version of the classification criteria (the concept definitions deciding what 'supports' means) the labels were made under.

criteria_locked_at.description: When those criteria were finalized. The first half of the order gate.

criteria_lock_content_hash.description: Content hash of the locked criteria, mirroring MethodProtocol.protocol_lock_content_hash's role: it pins WHICH criteria, not merely that some were locked.

criteria.description: The locked criteria themselves, carried inline so a case can be re-judged without a second file: category name -> its binding definition. Every declared category should appear.

labelled_at.description: When the labelling happened. MUST be strictly after criteria_locked_at — enforced by the loader, which refuses rather than warns. Criteria that move after the labels are a moving standard, which is the exact failure the ordering exists to prevent.

notes.description: Free-text remarks about the set as a whole — known limitations, sampling frame, anything a reader needs to judge what the number means.
